items.title: Global Phase Equivalence
items.statement: For square matrices $U,V$ of the same size, write $U\sim_{\mathrm{phase}}V$ when $U=\lambda V$ for some $\lambda\in\mathbb C$ with $|\lambda|=1$. This relation is kept distinct from exact matrix equality.

items.title: Demultiplexing a Two-Block Unitary
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space and let $U_0,U_1$ be unitary endomorphisms of $H$. On the control-first direct sum $H\oplus H$, the block unitary $\operatorname{diag}(U_0,U_1)$ factors as
$$\operatorname{diag}(U_0,U_1)=(I\otimes V)\operatorname{diag}(D,D^*)(I\otimes W)$$
for unitary $V,W$ on $H$ and a diagonal unitary $D$ in an orthonormal eigenbasis; $I\otimes V$ denotes $\operatorname{diag}(V,V)$ under $\mathbb C^2\otimes H\cong H\oplus H$.

items.title: Cayley Charts on the Unitary Matrix Group
items.statement:
For $N\ge1$, define $U(N)=\{Q\in M_N(\mathbb C):Q^*Q=QQ^*=I\}$ and $\mathfrak u(N)=\{X\in M_N(\mathbb C):X^*=-X\}$, both regarded as real spaces where appropriate. Then $U(N)$ is a compact smooth real manifold of dimension $N^2$. Near $I$, the Cayley map
$$X\longmapsto (I+X)(I-X)^{-1}$$
is a smooth chart from $\mathfrak u(N)$; left translates give a finite atlas. The Frobenius inner product induces a smooth Riemannian metric. Under AC$_\omega$, its volume density defines a normalized Borel volume probability $\mu_F$; a Borel subset is $\mu_F$-null exactly when its intersection with every chart has Lebesgue-null coordinate image. Under AC, $\mu_F$ is the normalized Haar probability, so this also gives the Haar-null criterion in that branch.
items.axiom_use: Assume AC_omega for the Radon volume measure; assume full AC only for the optional identification with normalized Haar probability.

items.title: Cosine-Sine Block Decomposition
items.statement:
Let $k\ge1$ and let $U\in U(2k)$ be partitioned into $k\times k$ blocks
$$U=\begin{pmatrix}A&B\\ C&D\end{pmatrix}.$$
There are block-diagonal unitaries $L=\operatorname{diag}(L_0,L_1)$ and $R=\operatorname{diag}(R_0,R_1)$ and nonnegative real diagonal matrices $C_0,S_0$ such that
$$U=L\begin{pmatrix}C_0&-S_0\\S_0&C_0\end{pmatrix}R,\qquad C_0^2+S_0^2=I,\quad 0\le C_0,S_0\le I.$$
The singular values at $0$ and $1$ are allowed, with no nondegeneracy assumption.

items.title: Two-Level Unitary
items.statement: Let a finite ordered register have an orthonormal computational basis $(|z\rangle)_{z\in\mathcal X}$, using the root convention that the inner product is linear in its first argument. For distinct labels $x,y\in\mathcal X$, choose $V\in U(2)$, where $U(2)=\{M\in M_2(\mathbb C):M^*M=MM^*=I_2\}$. The **two-level unitary** $T_{x,y}(V)$ acts by the matrix $V$ in the ordered basis $(|x\rangle,|y\rangle)$ and acts as the identity on $\operatorname{span}\{|x\rangle,|y\rangle\}^{\perp}$. Its action is exact matrix equality: any scalar phase contained in $V$ is retained.

items.title: Exact Two-Level Elimination of a Unitary
items.statement:
Input: an exact-arithmetic representation of $U\in U(N)$, $N\ge1$, supporting addition, multiplication, conjugation, nonnegative square roots, exact zero tests, and exact division by nonzero positive real scalars. Output: a finite ordered factorization into two-level unitaries and a diagonal unitary. This is an exact algebraic procedure; no claim of a bit-time algorithm for arbitrary real input is made.

Initialize $M:=U$ and an empty chronological list. For each column $j=0,\ldots,N-2$, and for $r=N-1,N-2,\ldots,j+1$, set $a=M_{r-1,j}$ and $b=M_{r,j}$. If $b=0$, do nothing. Otherwise set $h=\sqrt{|a|^2+|b|^2}>0$ and left-multiply rows $(r-1,r)$ by
$$G=\frac1h\begin{pmatrix}\overline a&\overline b\\-b&a\end{pmatrix},$$
recording this two-level unitary in the order applied. Let the resulting matrix be $D$. Return the factorization $U=G_1^*\cdots G_s^*D$. In chronological circuit order, apply $D$ first and then $G_s^*,\ldots,G_1^*$.

items.title: Correctness and Termination of Two-Level Elimination
items.statement: For $U\in U(N)$, the elimination procedure of [[alg-qc-two-level-unitary-elimination]] terminates after at most $N(N-1)/2$ Givens steps and returns an exact factorization of $U$ into the recorded two-level adjoints followed by a diagonal unitary. The number of diagonal entries is $N$; entries equal to $1$ need no phase gate.

items.title: One-Qubit Euler Decomposition
items.statement:
Use the rotation convention of [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]] and define $R_y(\theta):=R_{(0,1,0)}(\theta)$:
$$R_z(\alpha)=\begin{pmatrix}e^{-i\alpha/2}&0\\0&e^{i\alpha/2}\end{pmatrix},\qquad R_y(\theta)=\begin{pmatrix}\cos(\theta/2)&-\sin(\theta/2)\\\sin(\theta/2)&\cos(\theta/2)\end{pmatrix}.$$
For every $U\in U(2)$ there are real $\delta,\alpha,\theta,\beta$ with
$$U=e^{i\delta}R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta)R_z(\beta).$$
If $\det U=1$, the scalar factor is unnecessary and $U=R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta)R_z(\beta)$.

items.title: Exact Two-Qubit Cartan Decomposition
items.statement:
For every $U\in U(4)$ there are $A,B,C,D\in SU(2)$, real $a,b,c,\delta$, and the matrices
$$X=\begin{pmatrix}0&1\\1&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Y=\begin{pmatrix}0&-i\\i&0\end{pmatrix},\quad Z=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&-1\end{pmatrix}$$
such that
$$U=e^{i\delta}(A\otimes B)\exp\!\bigl(i(aX\otimes X+bY\otimes Y+cZ\otimes Z)\bigr)(C\otimes D).$$
The equality is exact; the scalar $e^{i\delta}$ is displayed.

items.title: Global Phase Under Control
items.statement:
Let $H$ be a nonzero finite-dimensional target space, let $U$ be unitary on $H$, and let $|\lambda|=1$. In control-first order put
$$C(U)=\begin{pmatrix}I_H&0\\0&U\end{pmatrix},\qquad P_\lambda=\begin{pmatrix}1&0\\0&\lambda\end{pmatrix}.$$
Then $C(\lambda U)=(P_\lambda\otimes I_H)C(U)$. A scalar multiplying an entire output leaves every defined finite-POVM outcome law unchanged, whereas a scalar attached to a target matrix inside a control gives a phase on only the active control block; applying $P_{\overline\lambda}$ on the control restores the exact controlled matrix.

items.title: Parameter Count for a Fixed CNOT Skeleton
items.statement: Assume AC$_\omega$ to form normalized Frobenius volume on $U(2^n)$. For fixed $n\ge1$ and a fixed ordered CNOT skeleton with $m$ CNOTs, arbitrary exact one-qubit gates, and no ancillas, the set of exact circuit matrices is contained in a finite union of smooth images of real parameter spaces of dimension at most $3n+4m+1$. If $3n+4m+1<4^n$, this fixed skeleton has measure zero. Under full AC, it is Haar-null.
items.axiom_use: AC_omega is assumed for the normalized smooth volume measure; full AC is needed only for the optional Haar identification.

items.title: Gray-Code Synthesis of a Multiplexed Axis Rotation
items.statement:
Let $k\ge0$ controls have computational labels $x\in\{0,1\}^k$, and let $\theta_x\in\mathbb R$. Fix $a\in\{x,y,z\}$. On one target qubit define
$$M=\sum_{x\in\{0,1\}^k}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes R_a(\theta_x),\qquad R_a(t)=\exp(-it\sigma_a/2).$$
Then $M$ is exactly synthesized with $2^k$ CNOTs for $k>0$ (the final CNOT restores the parity network). For $a=y,z$ it uses $2^k$ target rotations $R_a(\beta_j)$; for $a=x$ it uses $2^k$ $R_y$ rotations in the fixed target basis described below; for $k=0$ it is one rotation and no CNOT. For $a=x$ and $k>0$ the implementation also uses two fixed target basis-change gates; the $y,z$ implementations need none. One may replace the cyclic Gray traversal by a traversal that omits the final restoration and absorb that final parity into the next block only when that block is explicitly specified.

items.title: Exact Controlled One-Qubit Unitary with Two CNOTs
items.statement: For every $U\in U(2)$, the exact controlled matrix $C(U)=\operatorname{diag}(I_2,U)$ is realized with two CNOTs and one-qubit gates only. The scalar phase of $U$ is implemented as a phase gate on the control and is not discarded.

items.title: Exact Three-CNOT Synthesis of Two-Qubit Unitaries
items.statement: Every $U\in U(4)$ has an exact circuit with no ancillas, at most three CNOT gates, and arbitrary one-qubit gates. The scalar phase is implemented as a one-qubit scalar gate and is not discarded.

items.title: Two-CNOT Synthesis up to a Migrating Terminal Diagonal
items.statement: Every $U\in U(4)$ factors exactly as $U=\Delta V$, where $\Delta$ is diagonal in the ordered two-qubit computational basis and $V$ has a no-ancilla circuit with at most two CNOTs and arbitrary one-qubit gates. Scalar phases are retained. Consequently, if a chronological circuit has $N\ge1$ arbitrary two-qubit slots all on the same two wires and each separator preserves every computational label on those two wires, the slots can be synthesized using at most $2(N-1)+3$ CNOTs in total, leaving the separator operations unchanged. This counts only the slots' CNOTs.

items.title: Exact Central Controlled-Z Absorption at a QSD Node
items.statement: Let $k\ge1$, let the first of $k+1$ wires be the target, and let $L=\operatorname{diag}(L_0,L_1)$ and $R=\operatorname{diag}(R_0,R_1)$ be generic block-diagonal unitaries in that target's basis. Let $M$ be a multiplexed $R_y$ on that target, selected by the other $k$ wires. The exact matrix $LMR$ can be represented by four generic $k$-qubit slots, two multiplexed $R_z$ factors and a central network with only $2^k-1$ controlled-$Z$ gates and arbitrary one-qubit rotations. Each controlled-$Z$ costs one CNOT. Thus one CNOT is saved relative to demultiplexing $L,R$ and using a full $2^k$-CNOT central rotation. The exact rewritten factors add no workspace, preserve scalar phases, and keep every non-target wire a select wire within the central network.

items.title: Generic No-Ancilla CNOT Lower Bound
items.statement:
Assume AC$_\omega$ to form normalized Frobenius volume. For $n\ge1$, almost every $n$-qubit unitary with respect to that measure requires at least
$$\left\lceil\frac{4^n-3n-1}{4}\right\rceil$$
CNOT gates in an exact circuit with arbitrary one-qubit gates and no ancillas. Under full AC, normalized Frobenius volume is normalized Haar measure, so the same is a Haar-almost-everywhere bound. This is a generic lower bound and is not a per-unitary assertion.
items.axiom_use: Assume AC_omega for normalized Frobenius volume; assume full AC only for the optional identification with normalized Haar measure.

items.title: Linear Multicontrolled X with One Borrowed Wire
items.statement: For every integer $r\ge1$, an $r$-controlled $X$ on $r$ control wires and one target has an exact circuit of $O(r)$ arbitrary one-qubit gates and CNOTs when one additional borrowed wire is available. The circuit equals $C^r(X)\otimes I$ on the entire register: the borrowed wire is returned unchanged for every state, including states entangled with the controls, target, or an external register. No wire is initialized or measured.

items.title: Exact QSD CNOT Upper Bound
items.statement:
For $n\ge2$, every $n$-qubit unitary has an exact no-ancilla circuit with arbitrary one-qubit gates and at most
$$\frac{23}{48}4^n-\frac32 2^n+\frac43$$
CNOTs. For $n=1$, no CNOT is needed. For $n=0$, a circuit on the empty register realizes a scalar unitary exactly if and only if it is $1$; the empty circuit realizes this identity with no gates. This is a gate-count bound; it makes no numerical decomposition-time or finite-precision bit-complexity claim.

items.title: Multicontrolled Unitaries with and without a Clean Work Bit
items.statement:
For $m\ge1$ controls and exact $U\in U(2)$, define
$$C^m(U)=\sum_{x\ne1^m}|x\rangle\langle x|\otimes I_2+|1^m\rangle\langle1^m|\otimes U.$$
This controlled operation has (i) a no-workspace exact construction with $O(m^2)$ one-qubit and CNOT gates, and (ii) an exact construction using one clean work bit, initially $0$ and returned to $0$, with $O(m)$ such gates. For nonscalar $U$, every exact circuit needs at least $m$ two-qubit gates, also when auxiliary wires are allowed with data-independent initial state and exact clean or dirty return. Clean auxiliary wires start at $0$ and return to $0$ for every data input; dirty auxiliary wires may start in any state and the full operation is $C^m(U)\otimes I$ on them, including correlated inputs. A fixed auxiliary state may be internally entangled but is initially independent of the data. These are upper/lower bounds; the quadratic no-work construction is not asserted optimal.

items.title: Gray-Path Synthesis of a Two-Level Gate
items.statement:
Input distinct $x,y\in\{0,1\}^n$, $n\ge1$, exact $V\in U(2)$, and for each controlled call a choice between the no-workspace and clean-bit constructions of [[thm-qc-multicontrolled-ancilla-resource-tradeoff]]. If any call selects the clean-bit construction, supply one clean bit initialized to $0$. Output: the chronological elementary-gate list on the $n$ data wires and, if selected, that one clean work wire.

Let $g_0=x,\ldots,g_d=y$ be the path that flips the differing bit positions once in increasing order, where $d$ is the Hamming distance. For $j=0,\ldots,d-2$, swap $g_j$ and $g_{j+1}$ by an $X$ on their differing bit controlled on the other $n-1$ bits matching their common pattern. Apply $V$ to the final pair $g_{d-1},y$ by a one-qubit target gate controlled on their common other bits, reversing the ordered $2\times2$ block if $g_{d-1}$ has target bit $1$. Undo the swaps in reverse order. Expand every multi-control using its selected construction; implement negative controls by conjugating that control wire with $X$.

Expand the calls by the following procedures. Every list below is chronological; concatenation means execute the left list first. Order control wires and available spare wires by their register positions. All parameter selections are exact mathematical operations: use exact matrix arithmetic, a finite-dimensional unitary eigendecomposition, polar arguments and the Euler parameter selection of [[thm-qc-one-qubit-euler-decomposition]]. The input representation must support these selections and exact zero tests; no finite-precision bit-time claim is made. Fix each selection when its call is first expanded and retain the resulting list for an inverse call.

For one control $c$, target $t$ and matrix $W$, choose $W=e^{i\delta}R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta)R_z(\beta)$ as in [[thm-qc-one-qubit-euler-decomposition]]. Form the three matrices $A=R_z(\alpha)R_y(\theta/2)$, $B=R_y(-\theta/2)R_z(- (\alpha+\beta)/2)$ and $C=R_z((\beta-\alpha)/2)$. Define $S(c,t;W)$ to be the list $C_t$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{c\to t}$, $B_t$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{c\to t}$, $A_t$, $\operatorname{diag}(1,e^{i\delta})_c$. Each of $A,B,C$ is one arbitrary one-qubit gate, as in [[thm-qc-one-control-unitary-two-cnot]]. Define $T(a,b;t)$ by setting $J=((1+i)I+(1-i)X)/2$ and concatenating $S(b,t;J)$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{a\to b}$, $S(b,t;J^*)$, $\mathrm{CNOT}_{a\to b}$, $S(a,t;J)$.

Define the ladder list $L(c_1,\ldots,c_s;t)$ with an ordered supply of at least $\max\{s-2,0\}$ distinct spare wires. For $s=1$ emit one CNOT; for $s=2$ emit $T(c_1,c_2;t)$. For $s\ge3$, use the first $s-2$ spares $a_1,\ldots,a_{s-2}$. Set $T_1=T(c_1,c_2;a_1)$, $T_j=T(c_{j+1},a_{j-1};a_j)$ for $2\le j\le s-2$, and $H=T(c_s,a_{s-2};t)$. Concatenate $T_1,\ldots,T_{s-2},H,T_{s-2},\ldots,T_1$ and then $T_2,\ldots,T_{s-2},H,T_{s-2},\ldots,T_2$; the latter list is just $H$ when $s=3$. This is the borrowed ladder used in [[lem-qc-borrowed-bit-multicontrolled-x-linear]].

Define $D(C;t;z)$ for an ordered nonempty control set $C$ and a distinct borrowed wire $z$. With one or two controls use the corresponding ladder base case and leave $z$ unused. With $r\ge3$ controls split $C$ into its first $p=\lceil r/2\rceil$ controls $A$ and the remaining $q=\lfloor r/2\rfloor$ controls $B$. Let $F=L(A;z)$ use spares from $B\cup\{t\}$, and let $G=L(B\cup\{z\};t)$ use spares from $A$. Emit $F,G,F,G$, using the same parameter choices for repeated lists. The stated spare supplies have at least $p-2$ and $q-1$ wires, respectively.

Define the positive-control no-workspace expansion $N(C;t;W)$ recursively. If $C$ is empty, emit $W_t$. If it has one wire $c$, emit $S(c,t;W)$. Otherwise write $C=A\cup\{b\}$, with $b$ its last control. Choose an orthonormal eigendecomposition $W=R\operatorname{diag}(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)R^*$ by [[thm-complex-spectral-theorem-for-normal-endomorphisms]], choose polar angles $\lambda_j=\cos u_j+i\sin u_j$ by [[thm-polar-form-with-unique-principal-argument]], and set $Z=R\operatorname{diag}(\cos(u_1/2)+i\sin(u_1/2),\cos(u_2/2)+i\sin(u_2/2))R^*$. The addition formulas of [[thm-sine-and-cosine-addition-formulas]] specify these half-angle roots. Emit $S(b,t;Z)$, $D(A;b;t)$, $S(b,t;Z^*)$, $D(A;b;t)$, $N(A;t;Z)$. The last call has one fewer control and uses only its indicated wires.

For the positive-control clean-bit expansion with nonempty $C$ and clean wire $w$, emit $D(C;w;t)$, $S(w,t;W)$, and the reversed adjoint of that same $D$ list. With no controls emit $W_t$ and leave $w$ unused. These are the two constructions analyzed in [[thm-qc-multicontrolled-ancilla-resource-tradeoff]]. For a pattern control, conjugate the selected whole positive-control list by one $X$ on each zero-valued control, ordering each set of these $X$ gates by wire position. Reverse the ordered middle block by using $XVX$ as its single matrix parameter, not by adding target $X$ occurrences.

Use the selected literal elementary gate list for each call without deleting identity gates or cancelling neighboring gates. In the one-control base use the three target matrices and one control phase as four arbitrary one-qubit gates. Use the same choices and reversed adjoint gate lists for the return swaps. Reuse the supplied clean bit sequentially; each selected clean-bit construction returns it to $0$.

items.title: Correctness of Gray-Path Two-Level Synthesis
items.statement:
The algorithm of [[alg-qc-two-level-gate-to-elementary-gates]] realizes the exact two-level unitary on the ordered selected pair $(x,y)$ and fixes every other computational-basis vector. Write $d$ for their Hamming distance and $m=n-1$. Before expansion there are $2(d-1)$ pattern-controlled swaps and one pattern-controlled target block.

Here are exact post-expansion counts for its literal circuits. A cost pair $(c,q)$ counts CNOTs and arbitrary one-qubit gates, respectively; pairs are added componentwise and identity gate occurrences are retained. Define
$$E_1=(1,0),\quad E_2=(8,12),\quad E_s=(4s-8)(8,12)\quad(s\ge3),$$
$$B_1=(1,0),\quad B_2=(8,12),\quad B_r=2E_{\lceil r/2\rceil}+2E_{\lfloor r/2\rfloor+1}\quad(r\ge3).$$
For a positive $m$-controlled one-qubit call the no-workspace cost is
$$Q_0=(0,1),\quad Q_1=(2,4),\quad Q_m=Q_{m-1}+2B_{m-1}+(4,8)\quad(m\ge2),$$
and the selected one-clean-bit cost is $K_m=2B_m+(2,4)$ for $m\ge1$ (use $K_0=Q_0$ with no work bit). For each forward swap $j$, choose $S_j\in\{Q_m,K_m\}$, and for the middle block choose $T\in\{Q_m,K_m\}$. If $z_j$ and $z_V$ are the numbers of zero-valued controls in their patterns, the exact total pair is
$$2\sum_{j=0}^{d-2}\bigl(S_j+(0,2z_j)\bigr)+T+(0,2z_V).$$
Its sum of coordinates is the exact elementary gate count. All-no-workspace selection uses $n$ wires and $O(dn^2)$ gates; all-clean selection uses at most $n+1$ wires and $O(dn)$ gates. For mixed selections one clean bit suffices and is reused sequentially, returned to zero after each call. When $n=1$, the circuit is one arbitrary one-qubit gate with cost $(0,1)$ and no work bit.

title: Continuous-Gate Universality and Exact Synthesis — Examples

items.title: A Two-Level Rotation on Two Qubits
items.statement:
Use the ordered computational basis $|00\rangle,|01\rangle,|10\rangle,|11\rangle$. Select $x=00$, $y=01$, and
$$V=\frac1{\sqrt2}\begin{pmatrix}1&-1\\1&1\end{pmatrix}.$$
This is the QC7 rotation $R_y(\pi/2)$, with its exact sign convention recorded in [[def-qc-one-qubit-gate-alphabet-and-rotations]].
